column1: # destructive-guard — two tiers. `hard` (exit 2) has no approval path; `ask` turns the
# command into an explicit confirmation prompt. The two are worth separating in a fixture
# because they are different promises: a hard block says "never", an ask says "not without
# you". A suite comparing exit codes alone scores them identically, since both exit 2 and
# ask-at-exit-0 look like "the hook did something".
# This is a representative set, not exhaustive coverage of a large hook. Each block below
# pins one class, plus the false-positive defence for that class — the half that actually
# regresses, because widening a matcher is easy and re-checking its blast radius is not.
# --- hard: pushes to the default branch, every spelling ---
# --- allow: the same verb aimed somewhere it is allowed ---
# --- hard: a redirect, a second refspec, an option's value or an all-branches flag hides main from a first-refspec read ---
# --- the directory a bare push runs in: its own -C over a cd, a subshell's cd stays inside it ---
# --- a substitution in the -C, the remote or the refspec does not cut the push out of its own segment ---

column2: cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)" && git push -u origin HEAD
git push origin feature/my-branch $(echo x) main
cd {push_main} && git push --force-with-lease=main:$(git rev-parse origin/main) origin
cd {push_main} && git push -u origin "$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD)"

column1: # --- a cd behind a reserved word or a builtin prefix, pushd and popd, and a repository moved by --git-dir ---

column2: if cd {push_main}; then git push origin HEAD; fi
if cd {push_main}; then git push; fi
if true; then cd {push_main} && git push; fi
for i in 1; do cd {push_main}; git push; done
if cd {push_feature}; then git push; fi
export GIT_DIR={push_main}/.git && git push origin feature/my-branch

column1: # --- a push inside a shell string runs where this guard cannot follow, so a bare one must name its branch ---
# --- an escaped space, an option that takes its value as the next word, and a tags-only push ---
# --- git accepts any unique prefix of a long option and bundled short flags ---
# --- an arithmetic expansion or a case pattern inside a subshell does not close the subshell ---

column2: (cd {push_main}; case x in x) true;; esac; git push)
case x in x) cd {push_main}; git push;; esac
case x in x) cd {push_feature}; git push;; esac
if true; then (cd {push_main} && git push); fi
cd {push_main} && case x in x) (cd {push_feature}; true); git push;; esac
cd {push_main} && case x in x) (cd {push_feature} && pwd); git push;; esac
cd {push_main} && (cd {push_feature}; case x in y) true;; esac); git push
cd {push_main} && (case x in x) cd {push_feature};; esac); git push
(cd {push_main}; case x in y) true;; esac); git push
case a in a|b) cd {push_main}; git push;; esac
case x in (x) cd {push_main};; esac; git push

column1: # --- an escaped parenthesis neither opens nor closes a subshell ---
# --- hard: merges. No merge grant is armed here (the setup points the grant store at an empty
# directory), so there is no approval path. test-merge-grant.py covers the armed turn. ---
# --- allow: reading a PR is not merging one ---
# --- allow: their read-only or non-destructive siblings ---
# --- allow: the trigger as message text rather than as an invocation. The commit that
# documents a rule must not be blocked by the rule it documents.

column2: git commit -m "docs: never git push origin main directly"
git commit -m "chore: remove the gh pr merge step from the runbook"

column1: # --- Command substitutions execute; single-quoted and escaped spellings remain data.
# WHY: a literal heredoc body remains data for a file-writing command.
# WHY: an interpreter executes the same heredoc body.
# WHY: shell wrappers preserve the interpreter ownership of standard input.
# WHY: negation changes status but not whether Bash executes its input.

column2:
if true; then bash <<'EOF'
git push origin main
EOF
fi

column1: # WHY: a quoted heredoc is executable when its command owns standard input.
# WHY: a non-interpreter command leaves its quoted heredoc body literal.

column2: bash -c true; cat <<'EOF'\ngit push origin main\nEOF

column1: # WHY: arguments after the delimiter still choose whether Bash reads standard input.
# WHY: wrappers pass a static -c payload to Bash for execution.

column3: env:bash,-c,git push origin main|bash:-c,git push origin main|git:push,origin,main

column1: # WHY: login-shell startup can change PATH, so this fixture is intentionally not an oracle probe.

column2: printf x; git commit -m 'bash -c git push origin main'
git commit -m "prefix $(git push origin main) suffix"
git commit -m "$(git status; git push origin main)"

column1: # WHY: an escaped inner legacy delimiter is syntax for a nested command substitution.
# WHY: nested legacy substitutions execute without double-quote context too.
# WHY: quoted data does not make a nested mutation an outer read.

column2: gh api -X GET "$(gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/42/merge)"

column1: # WHY: a nested quote must not hide the checkout after the substitution restores its directory.

column2: cd target && printf "$(printf "$(cd /)")" && git checkout main

column1: # WHY: a quoted nested substitution must not swallow the later outer mutation.

column2: gh api -X GET "repos/o/r/$(printf "$(printf path)")" && gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/42/merge

column1: # --- read flags must only exempt their own nested command, not a mutation beside it.

column2: git commit -m "$(gh api -X GET repos/o/r/pulls/42/merge; gh api -X PUT repos/o/r/pulls/42/merge)"

column1: # WHY: an unquoted heredoc expands substitutions before a non-interpreter receives data.
# WHY: legacy substitutions expand in the same unquoted body.
# WHY: quotes in an unquoted body do not suppress substitution.
# WHY: a quoted delimiter leaves its body literal.
# WHY: any quoted part of a delimiter leaves its body literal.
# WHY: an escaped delimiter also leaves its body literal.
# WHY: an escaped dollar stays literal in an unquoted body.
# WHY: tab-stripped heredocs still expand an unquoted body.
# WHY: every heredoc body expands before the command starts.

column2:
cat <<FIRST <<SECOND
$(git push origin main)
FIRST
$(git push origin main)
SECOND

column1: # WHY: here-strings perform command substitution before invocation.
# WHY: commands after a heredoc are separate executable commands.
# WHY: an ANSI-C quoted delimiter still terminates at its decoded word.
# WHY: a hex-escaped ANSI-C delimiter still terminates at its decoded word.
# WHY: a locale-translated delimiter still terminates at its decoded word.
# WHY: adjacent quoted fragments compose one delimiter word.
# WHY: an escaped body newline does not stop the next delimiter from terminating the heredoc.
# WHY: arithmetic shifts are not heredoc openers.
# --- Intentional conservative overmatch: a comment is inspected as shell-like text.
# --- A substitution-local cd cannot change the outer checkout directory.
# --- input unavailable: the extraction returns nothing, which is indistinguishable from
# "no command to guard". Pinned so a later edit cannot flip it silently.
